artifact_revision: agentmux 4e8b6136 + session-17 working tree (uncommitted). Agent Mux.app 0.1.0 Release, built and signed on the MacBook Pro by `just mac-app Release` through the remote route from the synced working tree; bundled amx 0.8.0 (revision 4e8b6136951d-dirty, sha256:fda676b051d6); bundled tmux 3.7c runtime built from pinned sources (libevent 2.1.13-stable, ncurses 6.6, utf8proc 2.12.0, jemalloc 5.4.0; arm64, min macOS 14.0; bin/tmux sha256 fb421000337b…, SHA256SUMS sha256 858d25c2c2d4f810…); embedded Ghostty 1.3.1
method: One recorded live run from a fresh world, eight cases in order (install bundle signed diagnostics update server uninstall down): 107 checks, 0 failed (session-17/install-acceptance.log ends 'RESULT: 107 passed, 0 failed'). Everything under test ran on Seb's MacBook Pro (macOS 27.0.1, arm64), by the operator's rule that no UI runs on the Studio: the Release bundle was built there, installed there by macos/scripts/install-app.sh into a disposable install root (/tmp/amxs17/Applications, never /Applications), run there with HOME and TMPDIR of its own, updated and uninstalled there by the same scripts. That Mac had no tmux anywhere, no Agent Mux.app and no preferences for it. The Studio only sent scripts over SSH and read results back; no input was synthesized on either machine and no window was opened or driven. Agents were stand-ins that count once a second, so 'the same agent, undisturbed' is the process's PID and start time, its registry record, and a count with no restart, skip or pause. Two earlier passes are not the record: the first exposed driver faults only (a path compared without /private; a 'standalone' amx that shared the world's TMPDIR and so launched into the live server), plus one product refinement made before the record (amx backend status now reports a missing tmux as a warning while a running server can still take launches); the second failed one check on an empty preferences domain left by `defaults delete`, after which the uninstaller also removes the plist. Supporting runs: the hosted suite on the MacBook (377 tests, 0 failures) and the Go suites on the Studio.
limits: The MacBook has no signing certificate (`security find-identity`: 0 valid identities), so the bundle is ad-hoc signed: the run shows the bundle, its amx and its tmux are sealed and verify, and that an altered bundle is refused; it does not show a Developer ID signature or notarization, which sign.sh applies only when given such an identity. The installer ran with AMX_APP_NO_LAUNCH=1 and the driver opened the app itself with the world's environment, so the installer's own final `open` was not exercised. The update's tmux executable is byte-identical to the first; only the runtime's VERSION (hence its checksums and install directory) differs. macOS 14-26 were not tested: the runtime is built with minos 14.0 and that was read from the binary, not run on such a system.

clean-supported-mac-install.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case clean-supported-mac-install, 17 checks, 0 failed). On Seb's MacBook Pro (macOS 27.0.1, arm64) with no tmux on the user's login PATH, in the world, or under /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/local, no Agent Mux.app, no preferences domain, and no session server, runtime or registry, `install-app.sh` exited 0 and printed `Installed /tmp/amxs17/Applications/Agent Mux.app`, leaving a whole bundle and nothing staged beside it, with the tmux runtime already installed under the data directory. The app started from the install root logged `running …/Agent Mux.app/Contents/Resources/bin/amx (bundled)` and `backend: tmux 3.7c (bundled with Agent Mux, verified)`. A daemon started with the bundled amx brought the app's feed to `live`; `amx project launch alpha --backend tmux --json` from the bundled amx exited 0 with backend tmux and runtime session rs-80c5335051bd7aa98ba282f30edcd805, the agent (pid 29002) counted, and the daemon's snapshot listed it. Nothing but the bundle was installed on that Mac.

bundled-tmux-and-libraries.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case bundled-tmux-and-libraries, 10 checks, 0 failed). `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` passed for all seven files of the runtime in the installed bundle and again for the copy amx installed at ~/.local/share/agent-mux/runtime/tmux-3.7c-858d25c2c2d4f810. `otool -L` on the bundled tmux listed only /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib and /usr/lib/libresolv.9.dylib: libevent 2.1.13-stable, ncurses 6.6, utf8proc 2.12.0 and jemalloc 5.4.0 are linked into it (named in VERSION, their five license files beside it). It reported `tmux 3.7c`, arm64, `minos 14.0`. `amx backend status --json` gave source bundled, verified true, version 3.7c, path the installed copy. The running session server (pid 29001) was executing that installed copy, not a file inside the app, and the record beside its socket named the same file; `vmmap` on it named `malloc zone jemalloc_zone_0x105047088`. The Mac had no other tmux to fall back on.

signed-bundle.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case signed-bundle, 10 checks, 0 failed). `codesign --verify --strict --deep --verbose=2` on the installed bundle printed `valid on disk` and `satisfies its Designated Requirement`; the app, its amx and its tmux each verified on their own under identifiers io.github.sglavoie.agentmux, .cli and .tmux, and Resources/tmux/SHA256SUMS is listed in the bundle's CodeResources. The signature is ad-hoc (`Signature=adhoc`, TeamIdentifier not set; the Mac has 0 signing identities), so this is integrity, not publisher identity. Three altered copies were offered to install-app.sh and each was refused with exit 1 and nothing installed: tmux with one byte appended (`does not match its checksums`), a sealed resource changed (`a sealed resource is missing or invalid … does not pass signature verification`), and tmux altered with its checksums rewritten to match (refused by the seal). amx pointed directly at an altered runtime reported `bin/tmux does not match its checksum`, `tmux: not available`, and installed nothing.

dependency-failure-diagnostics.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case dependency-failure-diagnostics, 12 checks, 0 failed). A standalone amx with no bundle, no installed runtime, no session server and no tmux on PATH: `amx backend status` exited 0 and printed `tmux: not available (need 3.5 or newer)`, each place tried (`bundled runtime: not present …`, `PATH: tmux not found`) and the fix (`Install tmux 3.5 or newer (`brew install tmux`), set [defaults.tmux] path in config.toml, or run Agent Mux.app, which bundles one.`); `--check --json` exited 1 with code tmux_unavailable; `amx project launch alpha --backend tmux` failed in JSON with code backend_unavailable and in text with the same places and fix, and started and registered nothing. A tmux 3.3a on PATH was refused as `tmux 3.3a is older than 3.5`; `[defaults.tmux] path = /nonexistent/tmux` was the only candidate tried (`not an executable file`) even with the bundled runtime offered; `launch_backend = "ghostty"` was reported with its value and `amx config validate`. The app, given AMX_TMUX=/nonexistent/tmux through its environment preference, logged `backend: warning tmux_unavailable: Agents can be launched while the running server lasts, but no tmux was found to start another one …`, `AMX_TMUX (/nonexistent/tmux): not an executable file` and the brew hint (a warning rather than an error because a session server was running with its own tmux), and returned to `tmux 3.7c (bundled with Agent Mux, verified)` once the preference was removed. The agent launched earlier counted through all of it without a gap.

update-preserves-agent.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case update-preserves-agent, 16 checks, 0 failed). With the app running (pid 30009, version 0.1.0) and agent alpha detached (no tmux client) as pid 29002 started 18:21:29 UTC, `install-app.sh` was given a second bundle (version 0.1.1, signed by sign.sh, tmux runtime SHA256SUMS bddf340e… instead of 858d25c2…). It exited 0 and printed `A session server is running with 1 agent(s); it is left running.`, `Quitting the running Agent Mux.app...`, `Updated /tmp/amxs17/Applications/Agent Mux.app`, `The session server is unchanged (29001-1791656489); 1 agent(s) running.` Afterwards the installed bundle was 0.1.1 and passed strict deep verification with nothing staged beside it, the old app process was gone, the agent was the same process (same PID and start time), its registry record was identical (live, pane %0, pid 29002, same generation), and its own count ran 35 → 44 across the update with no restart, no skipped number and no two counts more than 3 s apart. The updated app started on its bundled amx, its feed went live carrying the same runtime session, and `amx attach rs-80c5… --json` from the updated bundle returned state live, pid 29002, clients 0. The daemon (pid 28959) was also the same process.

live-server-not-replaced.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case live-server-not-replaced, 11 checks, 0 failed). After the update that shipped another tmux runtime, the session server was the same process (pid 29001, started 18:21:29 UTC), its generation 29001-1791656489 was unchanged, and `ps` showed it still executing …/runtime/tmux-3.7c-858d25c2c2d4f810/bin/tmux, which was still on disk and still matched its checksums. The update's runtime had been installed beside it (…/tmux-3.7c-bddf340e84175725, now `current`), not over it, and the record beside the socket still named the server's own executable. `amx backend status` from the updated bundle printed `server tmux: …858d25c2c2d4f810/bin/tmux` and `info: The running server keeps the tmux it was started with … is used once its last agent has ended`, and the updated app logged `backend: info server_keeps_previous_tmux`. A second agent (beta, pid 30941) launched after the update ran in the same server under the same generation, and alpha kept counting without a gap. In the uninstall case, once that server had been ended on request, the next server started from the bddf340e runtime. The installer itself compares the generation before and after and exits nonzero if it differs; here it printed that it was unchanged.

uninstall-preserves-data.evidence: Observed in session-17/install-acceptance.log (case uninstall-preserves-data, 26 checks, 0 failed).
